official_title: THIS IS A TAX INCREASE; the issuance of bonds in the amount of $260,000,000 for citywide park, recreation, aquatic, and open space improvements, and the levy of taxes sufficient to pay the principle of and interest in bonds.
plain_summary: Lets the city borrow up to $260 million for parks: $65.5M buildings, $29.5M infrastructure, $65M parkland improvements, $65M pools and aquatics, $35M land purchases. Named sites include Zilker, four pool rebuilds, trails, and a District 6 recreation center.
yes_means: A YES vote lets the city sell $260 million in bonds for parks and repay them with property taxes.
no_means: A NO vote means the city cannot sell these bonds; parks projects would need other funding or wait for a later election.
current_law: No parks bond is currently authorized; the last comprehensive city bond was 2018.
fiscal_impact: City estimate: up to $8.14 per year per $100,000 of a homestead's appraised value (LWV). The Statesman reports the combined A and B package costs a typical homeowner more than $40 a year once the debt is issued, likely around 2033. Council approved it 8-3 over staff advice to wait until 2028.
confusing_wording_note: Texas law makes every bond ballot start with "THIS IS A TAX INCREASE." That is required language, not a judgment about the size of the increase. Vote FOR to approve the borrowing, AGAINST to reject it.

supporters_case.text: Supporters, including the Austin Chronicle, Labor Council and AURA, say parks and pools have deferred maintenance that only gets more expensive, and the departments are well run.

opponents_case.text: Opponents, including Mayor Watson and Council Members Velásquez and Duchen, cited affordability and city financial policy; candidate Jeffery Bowen points to $700 million in existing deferred park maintenance.

official_title: THIS IS A TAX INCREASE; the issuance of bonds in the amount of $35,000,000 for library facilities and the levy of taxes sufficient to pay the principal of and interest on the bonds.
plain_summary: Lets the city borrow up to $35 million for libraries: about $20 million to renovate and expand the Hampton Branch at Oak Hill and $15 million for a new Colony Park Branch in Northeast Austin.
yes_means: A YES vote lets the city sell $35 million in bonds for library buildings and repay them with property taxes.
no_means: A NO vote means the city cannot sell these bonds for the two library projects.
current_law: No library bond is currently authorized.
fiscal_impact: City estimate: up to $1.10 per year per $100,000 of a homestead's appraised value (LWV).
confusing_wording_note: Texas law makes every bond ballot start with "THIS IS A TAX INCREASE." That is required language, not a judgment about the size of the increase. Vote FOR to approve the borrowing, AGAINST to reject it.

supporters_case.text: Supporters say the Oak Hill branch is overdue for expansion and Colony Park has no library.

opponents_case.text: Opponents object to adding debt while the city budget is tight.

official_title: Shall the City Charter be amended to clarify that the Independent Citizens Redistricting Commission (ICRC) is independent of City Council control, allow the ICRC to review City districts after changes to the City's boundary lines, create voter registration and residency duration exceptions for student members, provide an effective date for the redistricting plan adopted by the ICRC, increase the number of individuals in the pool of potential appointees to the ICRC, clarify the method and timing of filling vacancies on the ICRC, and allow City staff to communicate with the ICRC outside of a meeting as long as such communication is in compliance with the Texas Open Meetings Act?
plain_summary: Updates the rules for the citizen commission that draws Austin's 10 council districts: says it is independent of council, lets it redraw after annexations, lets college students serve, and tidies up appointments, vacancies and staff contact.
yes_means: A YES vote makes these changes to how the redistricting commission works.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current commission rules.
current_law: The ICRC was created by voters in 2012. The charter does not currently let it act after boundary changes or let students who have not met residency rules serve.

supporters_case.text: The Chronicle: the process was always meant to be independent of political control and the other changes sound beneficial.

official_title: Shall the City Charter be amended to delete language providing that the City Council shall meet at least once each week?
plain_summary: Removes the charter rule that council must meet at least once a week, letting council set its own meeting schedule.
yes_means: A YES vote removes the weekly meeting requirement.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the requirement that council meet at least once a week.
current_law: The charter requires at least one council meeting per week.

opponents_case.text: The Chronicle opposes: "So that they can do even more of their business off the dais, out of public view?"

official_title: Shall the City Charter be amended to delete language requiring the City Council to determine its rules and order of business by ordinance?
plain_summary: Removes the rule that council must adopt its meeting rules by ordinance (a formal public vote on a local law). Council could set rules another way, such as a resolution.
yes_means: A YES vote removes the ordinance requirement for council meeting rules.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the requirement that meeting rules be adopted by ordinance.
current_law: The charter requires council rules and order of business to be set by ordinance.

opponents_case.text: The Chronicle opposes for the same reason as Prop D: less open process.

official_title: Shall the City Charter be amended to clarify the meaning of the term "election" and to provide that the campaign contribution and expenditure limits shall be modified each year by January 1st instead of with the adoption of the budget?
plain_summary: Clarifies which elections (general, runoff, special) the city's campaign money limits apply to, and moves the yearly inflation update of those limits to January 1 instead of budget time in August.
yes_means: A YES vote makes these campaign finance housekeeping changes.
no_means: A NO vote leaves the current wording and timing.
current_law: Limits are updated when the budget is adopted, usually in August.

official_title: Shall the City Charter be amended to provide that initiative elections and petitioned charter amendment elections must be held on the next available November election date that occurs in an even-numbered year and that allows sufficient time to comply with other requirements of law?
plain_summary: Requires citizen-petition measures (initiatives and petitioned charter amendments) to go on the ballot in November of an even-numbered year, when turnout is highest, rather than the next available election date.
yes_means: A YES vote moves citizen-petition elections to even-year Novembers only.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current schedule, which can put petition measures on May or odd-year ballots.
current_law: Petition measures go to the next available uniform election date, which can be a low-turnout May or odd-year November election.
confusing_wording_note: A YES vote can mean a longer wait before voters decide on a petition. Supporters say more people vote in even years; critics say petitions get buried at the bottom of a long ballot.

supporters_case.text: More voters weigh in during even-year November elections.

opponents_case.text: The Chronicle split "Yes and No": issues get less scrutiny at the end of a long ballot.

official_title: Shall the City Charter be amended to provide that the City Council appoints and removes the City Attorney?
plain_summary: Moves the power to hire and fire the City Attorney from the city manager to the elected City Council.
yes_means: A YES vote gives council the power to appoint and remove the City Attorney.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the city manager in charge of hiring and firing the City Attorney.
current_law: The city manager appoints the City Attorney.

supporters_case.text: The Chronicle: better that city legal staff answer to elected officials who answer to voters.

official_title: Shall the City Charter be amended to require an Independent Affordability and Efficiency Initiative on a regular basis and before any tax rate increase election and requiring the independent contractor to identify annual and multi-year savings that exceed the cost of the contractor's service?
plain_summary: A citizen petition from Save Austin Now. It would write into the charter a recurring outside review of city spending and efficiency: first review within a year of hiring the contractor, then every five years, and one must be finished in the year before any election to raise the city's operating tax rate. The contractor must commit to finding savings bigger than its fee.
yes_means: A YES vote adds the mandatory outside review to the City Charter, where only voters can change it.
no_means: A NO vote does not add it; the city's existing auditor and the council-approved efficiency assessment continue.
current_law: Austin has a City Auditor's office and, since February 2026, a council-approved Comprehensive Efficiency Assessment with an outside contractor (contract up to $5.23 million over several years). Those can be changed by council.
fiscal_impact: No official estimate. Opponents say each review could cost $5 million or more; Save Austin Now's attorney cites a Houston audit that cost $580,000.
confusing_wording_note: This is the one Austin proposition that is contested along political lines. The ballot wording ("Affordability and Efficiency Initiative") does not say "audit" or name Save Austin Now. Supporters call it an independent audit; opponents call it "DOGE for Austin."

supporters_case.text: Save Austin Now: City Hall has a $6.6 billion budget and voters rejected last year's tax increase; put independent scrutiny with deadlines into the charter so council cannot repeal it.

opponents_case.text: Six council members, labor groups and Rep. Casar say the review duplicates audits already under way and pays a consultant only if it finds cuts, which rewards cutting services.

official_title: Shall the City Charter be amended to make non-substantive corrections of typographical errors, punctuation, and sentence structure, and to change or remove language that is moot or unenforceable because it has been superseded by state law or by a final court order?
plain_summary: Cleans up typos, punctuation and dead language in the charter. The city says it makes no policy change.
yes_means: A YES vote makes the clean-up edits.
no_means: A NO vote leaves the charter text as is.

supporters_case.text: The Chronicle: no policy impact and no reason to oppose it.

jurisdiction: Austin Community College District (voters in the Pflugerville ISD area not already in ACC)
official_title: THIS IS A TAX INCREASE. Approving the annexation by the Austin Community College District of the following territory: the territory in the Pflugerville Independent School District that is not already within the Austin Community College taxing district, and authorizing the imposition of an ad valorem tax for junior college purposes, which is currently set at a rate of $0.1034, per $100 valuation of taxable property.
plain_summary: Only voters in the Pflugerville ISD area that is outside ACC's taxing district vote on this. If it passes, that area joins ACC: residents pay ACC's property tax (currently $0.1034 per $100 of value) and get in-district tuition and the free-tuition program for local high school graduates.
yes_means: A YES vote adds the Pflugerville ISD area to the ACC taxing district: ACC property tax starts, in-district tuition and ACC board voting rights follow.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the area outside ACC; residents keep paying out-of-district tuition and no ACC tax.
current_law: Pflugerville ISD voters rejected ACC annexation in past elections. Residents petitioned (5%+ of voters) to put it back on the ballot; ACC's board accepted the petition unanimously.
fiscal_impact: ACC tax at $0.1034 per $100: about $414 a year on a $400,000 taxable value before exemptions. ACC says it takes no position.
confusing_wording_note: This measure appears only on Pflugerville-area ballots. Austin voters will not see it.

supporters_case.text: The Statesman endorsed FOR: lower tuition and wider access to job training make annexation a smart investment for Pflugerville despite the higher tax bill.

opponents_case.text: Opponents object to a new permanent property tax on top of PfISD and city taxes.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to authorize monthly compensation for members of the City Council in the amount of seven hundred fifty dollars ($750.00) per month for the Mayor and five hundred dollars ($500.00) per month for Council Members?
plain_summary: Pays the mayor $750 a month and council members $500 a month. They are unpaid now, except expense reimbursement.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.
current_law: Council is unpaid; expenses can be reimbursed.
confusing_wording_note: Pflugerville has 14 charter amendments, A through N, each voted separately. They came from the charter review committee appointed in November 2025.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to add a new section requiring the City Council to adopt protections governing the collection, use, retention, and oversight of data, facial recognition, and surveillance technologies, to establish transparent approval processes for such technologies, and to require a responsible artificial intelligence framework?
plain_summary: Requires council to adopt rules on city data, facial recognition, surveillance tech and AI use, with a public approval process.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.
current_law: No charter requirement exists; council ended its Flock license-plate camera contract by vote.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to revise the procedures for adopting ordinances, including eliminating the requirement that a proposed ordinance be read at two Council meetings and instead requiring an additional reading only when the City Council determines that an amendment substantively changes the ordinance, and revising related notice and public-availability procedures?
plain_summary: Lets council pass most ordinances in one meeting instead of two, with a second reading only if it is substantively changed.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.
current_law: Ordinances must be read at two meetings.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to lower, from fifteen percent (15%) to ten percent (10%), the percentage of qualified voters required to sign a petition for an initiative, referendum, or nonbinding referendum?
plain_summary: Makes citizen petitions easier: 10% of voters instead of 15%.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to revise City Council meeting and agenda procedures, including requiring that an item submitted by a Council Member with the support of a second Council Member be placed on an agenda within sixty (60) days, requiring the Mayor to include such items on the agenda, and clarifying the Council's meetings requirements with City-created boards and commissions?
plain_summary: Any two council members can force an item onto an agenda within 60 days; the mayor must include it.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to provide that voter petition requirements be completed in compliance with state law and extending, from two (2) weeks to four (4) weeks, the deadline to file a supplementary petition after a petition is certified insufficient?
plain_summary: Gives petitioners four weeks instead of two to fix a petition that falls short.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.
current_law: Two weeks to supplement a petition.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to revise the requirements governing the development and content of the City's annual budget, including requiring that the City Manager prepare and present the budget in accordance with Government Finance Officers Association budget-award guidelines, requiring comparative budget information and a five-year financial forecast, and to add a new charter section requiring a publicly accessible reporting system and final close-out reports for major capital projects?
plain_summary: Requires a GFOA-standard budget, a five-year forecast, and public close-out reports on big capital projects.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to authorize the mayor alone to excuse the City Manager from attending a meeting?
plain_summary: Lets the mayor alone excuse the city manager from a council meeting.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to allow City Council to appoint residents of the city's ETJ as non-voting advisory participants on city boards and commissions?
plain_summary: Lets people who live just outside city limits (the ETJ) sit on city boards as non-voting advisers.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to provide that the Mayor and City Council set the strategic direction and general policy framework of the City?
plain_summary: States in the charter that the mayor and council set the city's strategic direction and policy.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to allow public comment during removal proceedings without requiring City Council approval?
plain_summary: Allows public comment at hearings to remove an official without a council vote to allow it.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to remove the requirement that the Municipal Court Judge reside within the City?
plain_summary: Drops the rule that the municipal judge must live in Pflugerville.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.
current_law: Judge must live in the city.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to add a new Section 11.05 specifying how the public may participate in City Council meetings, including the submission of written comments on agenda items and participation by remote communication to the extent permitted by state law?
plain_summary: Writes public-participation rules into the charter, including written comments and remote participation where state law allows.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.

official_title: Shall the City of Pflugerville City Charter be amended to make non-substantive technical and conforming corrections, including standardizing capitalization throughout the Charter; adopting language conforming with state law, and amending or deleting language that is unnecessary or duplicative of state law?
plain_summary: Technical clean-up of the charter text.
yes_means: A YES vote makes this charter change.
no_means: A NO vote keeps the current charter language.

jurisdiction: Round Rock ISD (Williamson and Travis counties)
official_title: THIS IS A TAX INCREASE Ratifying the ad valorem tax rate of $0.9484 per $100 valuation in Round Rock Independent School District for the current year, a rate that will result in an increase of 3.09 percent in maintenance and operations tax revenue for the District for the current year as compared to the preceding year, which is an additional $12,313,099.
plain_summary: Asks Round Rock ISD voters to approve a total tax rate of $0.9484 per $100, which raises operating revenue 3.09% (about $12.3 million) over last year.
yes_means: A YES vote approves the $0.9484 rate and the extra $12.3 million for operations.
no_means: A NO vote rolls the rate back to the voter-approval rate; the district loses the $12.3 million.
fiscal_impact: An additional $12,313,099 in M&O revenue for the district.
confusing_wording_note: A VATRE (voter-approval tax rate election) asks voters to ratify a school tax rate above the state cap. The 'tax increase' is in maintenance-and-operations revenue; your bill depends on your appraised value and exemptions.

official_title: THIS IS A TAX INCREASE. Ratifying the ad valorem tax rate of $1.1169 per $100 valuation in Leander Independent School District for the current year, a rate that will result in an increase of 3.72 percent in maintenance and operations tax revenue for the District for the current year as compared to the preceding year, which is an additional $12,066,324.
plain_summary: Asks Leander ISD voters to approve a $1.1169 rate, raising operating revenue 3.72% (about $12.1 million).
yes_means: A YES vote approves the rate and the extra $12.1 million.
no_means: A NO vote rolls the rate back; the district loses the $12.1 million.
confusing_wording_note: A VATRE (voter-approval tax rate election) asks voters to ratify a school tax rate above the state cap. The 'tax increase' is in maintenance-and-operations revenue; your bill depends on your appraised value and exemptions.

official_title: THIS IS A TAX INCREASE. Ratifying the ad valorem tax rate of $1.0328 per $100 valuation in Del Valle Independent School District for the current year, a rate that will result in an increase of 19.5% percent in maintenance and operations tax revenue for the District for the current year as compared to the preceding year, which is an additional $20,038,349.
plain_summary: Asks Del Valle ISD voters to approve a $1.0328 rate, raising operating revenue 19.5% (about $20 million).
yes_means: A YES vote approves the rate and the extra $20 million.
no_means: A NO vote rolls the rate back; the district loses the $20 million.
confusing_wording_note: A VATRE (voter-approval tax rate election) asks voters to ratify a school tax rate above the state cap. The 'tax increase' is in maintenance-and-operations revenue; your bill depends on your appraised value and exemptions.

official_title: THIS IS A PROPERTY TAX INCREASE; the issuance of bonds in the amount of $391,500,000 for (1) school facilities, including campus renovations and district-wide safety and security upgrades, and (2) buses, and the levy of taxes sufficient to pay the principal of and interest on the bonds.
plain_summary: A $391.5 million bond for Manor ISD campus renovations, safety upgrades and buses.
yes_means: A YES vote approves the bonds.
no_means: A NO vote rejects them.
confusing_wording_note: Texas law makes every bond ballot start with "THIS IS A TAX INCREASE." That is required language, not a judgment about the size of the increase. Vote FOR to approve the borrowing, AGAINST to reject it.

official_title: THIS IS A PROPERTY TAX INCREASE; the issuance of bonds in the amount of $8,500,000 for school technology improvements and the levy of taxes sufficient to pay the principal of and interest on the bonds.
plain_summary: An $8.5 million bond for Manor ISD technology.
yes_means: A YES vote approves the bonds.
no_means: A NO vote rejects them.
confusing_wording_note: State law requires technology bonds to be a separate proposition from facilities bonds.
